title:
Salvage Ultrasound-Guided Robot-Assisted Video-Endoscopic Inguinal Lymphadenectomy (RAVEIL) as Metastasis-Directed Therapy (MDT) in Oligoprogressive Metastatic Castration-
Resistant Prostate Cancer (mCRPC): A Case Report and Review of the Literature
content: Background: Metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer (mCRPC) represents a chal-lenging clinical entity due to its progression despite androgen-deprivation therapy (ADT). Current systemic treatments for mCRPC include androgen receptor inhibitors (e.g., en-zalutamide, abiraterone with prednisone), chemotherapy (e.g., docetaxel, cabazitaxel), bone-targeted therapies such as radium-223, and, in selected cases, PARP inhibitors for patients with homologous recombination repair (HRR) mutations. While these therapies prolong survival, they are often associated with resistance, adverse effects, and limited durability. Metastasis-directed therapies (MDTs), such as stereotactic ablative radiothera-py (SABR), have shown promise in oligometastatic settings, but their role in oligoprogres-sive mCRPC remains underexplored. Surgical approaches, including salvage lymphade-nectomy, are rarely pursued due to invasiveness and limited supporting data. This case report illustrates the potential of salvage robot-assisted video-endoscopic inguinal lym-phadenectomy (RAVEIL) in managing oligoprogressive mCRPC, offering a novel ap-proach to delay systemic progression. Methods: A 47-year-old male, initially diagnosed with metastatic hormone-sensitive prostate cancer (Gleason score 10), was treated with ADT, docetaxel chemotherapy, and underwent radical prostatectomy with super-extended pelvic lymph node dissection (sePLND) and retroperitoneal lymph node dissection (RPLND). Upon progression to oligoprogressive mCRPC, 68Ga-PSMA PET/CT identified a single metastatic inguinal lymph node. Salvage RAVEIL was performed using the da Vinci X™ Surgical System, guided by preoperative mapping to ensure precise removal of the metastatic node. Results: Histopathological examination confirmed metastatic involve-ment in one of the eight excised lymph nodes. Postoperatively, the patient achieved unde-tectable PSA levels, with prolonged biochemical progression-free survival. Minor compli-cations, including mild lymphorrhea and cellulitis, were successfully managed without impacting recovery. Importantly, no further metastatic progression was observed during a 14-month follow-up period, highlighting the efficacy of the intervention. Conclusions: This case underscores the clinical utility of RAVEIL as an MDT in oligoprogressive mCRPC, highlighting its potential to extend progression-free intervals while minimizing systemic treatment. As the first report of robotic surgery employed as MDT in this context, it sets a precedent for exploring it’s role within multimodal MDT strategies for advanced prostate cancer. Future research should validate these findings and further define the role of robotic surgery in mCRPC management.
